svg.text: A practical workflow using the Ames Housing Dataset
to create inputs that represent useful patterns.
BIG PICTURE | Follow the workflow left → right
Arrow = next workflow step. Engineered features are candidates; training/evaluation comes later.
• Start with df.info(), df.shape, df.head(); keep df.copy().
• Remove row IDs PID and Order from predictive inputs.
• Demo: fill one missing Garage Cars value with 0.
Median/mean considered; impute by meaning, not one rule.
• Check target skew, feature–target shape, and
correlations with histograms and pair plots.
• Apply np.log1p to selected skewed input features.
• SalePrice is described as right-skewed, but the
• Curvature around Overall Qual motivates squares.
• drop_first=True is shown for House Style.
• Add powers of existing variables to model curves.
• OQ2 = Overall Qual²; GLA2 = Gr Liv Area².
• With 2 inputs, it returns original terms, squares,
a cross-product, and an intercept by default.
• Extra features do not guarantee better accuracy.
• Interaction: multiply features to test whether one
• OQ × Year Built: candidate quality premium by age.
• Ratio: OQ ÷ Lot Area captures quality relative to lot.
• These are hypotheses motivated by the data—not
proven improvements. Keep only if evaluation helps.
• Pair plots / domain reasoning motivate candidates.
• Compare a value with its own group’s mean/spread.
• Examples: Year Built within House Style; Overall
• groupby() + transform() returns one statistic per row
and keeps the original row count.
• z < 0: below group mean; z > 0: above it.
Added • illustrative arithmetic (not a source-data result): x = 20, group mean = 15,
Interpretation: this value is 1 standard deviation above its category mean.
Six output columns total, including the intercept and both original inputs.
LOG transform → changes a value’s scale/distribution.
POLYNOMIAL x² → adds curvature for one variable.
INTERACTION x₁×x₂ → models a possible joint effect.
RATIO x₁/x₂ → represents one feature relative to another.
• Don’t treat 4000 as a universal living-area cutoff.
• Don’t fill every missing value with zero by default.
• Rare-category encoding can greatly expand columns.
• Candidate features must be tested—not assumed useful.
• Zero group standard deviation is not addressed in source.
notebook uses count ≤ 8. Match notebook: inclusive.
⚠ “New feature” count wording conflicts; listed output
is 6 columns total, including intercept + originals.

TOP 5: Inspect/clean • explore first • encode categories • engineer candidates • evaluate later.
